list.heading: Processing Fee
list.topPara: Charged by the new lender (typically 0.5% to 2% of the loan amount).
list.para: 💡 Tip: Negotiate with the lender or look for promotional offers with waived processing fees.

list.heading: Foreclosure Charges
list.topPara: Some lenders may charge 2-5% of the outstanding loan for early closure.
list.para: 💡 Tip: Check if your existing lender offers zero foreclosure charges, especially if you have a floating interest rate.

list.heading: Legal & Valuation Fees
list.topPara: Costs for property verification and legal checks, which vary by lender.
list.para: 💡 Tip: Choose a lender that covers valuation and legal charges as part of the loan transfer process.

list.heading: Stamp Duty
list.topPara: Some states may require a nominal stamp duty for the loan agreement.
list.para: 💡 Tip: Verify with the lender if stamp duty is applicable in your state and factor it into cost calculations.

list.heading: Administrative Charges
list.topPara: Some lenders impose additional service or administrative fees.
list.para: 💡 Tip: Ask for a detailed fee breakdown upfront to avoid hidden costs.

list.heading: Insurance Charges
list.topPara: If the new lender requires a loan protection plan, this could add extra costs.
list.para: 💡 Tip: Check if existing insurance policies are transferable or compare third-party options for lower premiums.

thingsToConsider.heading: Things to Consider Before Transferring Your Loan

cards.heading: Right Time to Transfer
cards.para: The best time to transfer your plot loan is when interest rates drop or your financial situation improves, allowing better terms. Transferring early in the tenure maximizes interest savings. A strong credit score increases approval chances at lower rates.

cards.heading: Cost vs. Savings
cards.para: A balance transfer includes fees like processing, legal, and foreclosure charges. Compare the new EMI and interest with your current loan to calculate total savings. If transfer costs exceed savings, it may not be beneficial.

cards.heading: Top-Up Loan Option
cards.para: Some lenders offer a top-up loan with balance transfer, giving extra funds for construction or personal use. Check if the new lender provides this option and compare interest rates. Ensure the revised EMI and tenure stay within your budget before opting for it.

thingsYouShouldKnow.heading: Things you should know
paraGraph: Independent Facilitator: Digital DSA operates as an independent loan facilitator and web aggregator, bridging the gap between loan consumers and licensed banks or NBFCs. We are not an authorized financial institution and do not offer loans directly.

Loan Approval: The sole discretion of approving or rejecting a loan lies with the respective bank or NBFC where the user applies. Digital DSA does not guarantee loan approval or offer assurance from any specific bank or NBFC. All loans are subject to credit approval, and their terms, conditions, fees, and charges apply.

Liability: Digital DSA is not responsible for any loss, damage, or failure at the user’s end during loan processing. The final decision of the bank or NBFC is binding on both the user and Digital DSA.

Important Information: This information is provided without considering your personal objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please assess its suitability before acting. Exclusive offers are available only when you avail of a loan through Digital DSA and meet specific conditions.
